options.text: Because the zigzag path lengthens the effective wavelength along the guide.
Because the guide slows the wave so wavelength always matches free space.

Because guides only carry DC, not waves.

questions.explanation: The wave bounces at an angle, so the wavelength along the guide is longer than free-space wavelength. Cutoff and DC claims are wrong.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: What the characteristic impedance of a line is
questions.stem: Why is Z0 important in transmission line design?

options.text: It determines the load power rating.
It fixes the operating frequency.
It is the DC resistance of the line.
It sets the condition for no reflection when matched to load.

questions.explanation: Z0 determines the matching condition: when load equals Z0, reflection is zero. Power rating, DC resistance, and frequency are separate.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.stem: Stage 1: a line is matched. Stage 2: what follows?

options.text: Stage1 no; Stage2 always mismatched.
Stage1 yes; Stage2 total reflection.
Stage1 yes; Stage2 zero reflection and full power transfer.
Stage1 yes; Stage2 infinite VSWR.

questions.explanation: A matched line yields zero reflection and full power transfer. Total reflection and infinite VSWR are mismatch results.
